A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same dXPP research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–E are readable and can be reliably matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-accuracy experiments, projection and portfolio runtime benchmarks, and Sudoku learning and runtime results in Appendix E.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a smoothing-parameter sensitivity experiment in Section 4.1 and Table 2.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (9)–(13) retain the black-box QP solve, dual-scaled penalties, softplus smoothing and primal-dimensional backward system. Active-set pruning is unchanged. The added parameter sweep evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate random strictly convex QPs, simplex and chain projections, seven-ETF portfolio optimization, and Sudoku boards of sizes 4×4, 9×9 and 16×16. The smoothing sweep introduces no new dataset, task or input scenario.

E2.justification: Gradient accuracy uses dQP as reference; projection and portfolio comparisons retain dQP, OptNet, SCQPTH and CVXPYLayers; Sudoku retains dQP and OptNet. The added sensitivity study introduces no new comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds a smoothing sweep using δ proportional to ρδ times the KKT norm, rounded to the nearest power of ten, with ρδ from 10^-5 to 10^-9. Existing experiments retain their stated default δ=10^-6, penalty strength, data generation and solver settings.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 and new Table 2 add a focused sensitivity analysis across four random-QP sizes, testing how smoothing affects gradient accuracy. No corresponding sweep appears in v1. Existing Sudoku convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both report mean and standard deviation for the original gradient discrepancies over 50 random instances and retain the appendix averaging descriptions. New Table 2 follows the existing mean-and-standard-deviation practice without introducing a new uncertainty or significance procedure.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 1–5 retain their values as v3 Tables 1 and 3–6. New Table 2 adds smoothing-dependent discrepancies: for 5000×2000 QPs, mean error is 2.62×10^-7 at ρδ=10^-7, versus 3.18×10^-6 at 10^-5 and 1.63×10^-5 at 10^-9. These are additional settings, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The exact-penalty proposition, derivative decompositions, convergence theorem and proofs in Appendices A–D retain their mathematical substance and assumptions. Changed proposition numbering and definition symbols are presentational.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of solver-agnostic differentiation, a primal-dimensional SPD backward system, convergence to KKT sensitivity and scalable empirical performance. The additional experiment supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 newly explains the practical smoothing tradeoff: large δ introduces approximation bias, while very small δ increases numerical sensitivity, making an intermediate level preferable. Existing discussions of degeneracy, applicability and future extensions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an open-source implementation statement and repository address in the abstract, absent from v1. Appendix hardware, software, tolerances, data-generation and training details are retained. Repository contents or accessibility were not independently checked.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to KKT differentiation, solver-agnostic layers and penalty methods are retained. Author-year citations and bibliographic metadata updates do not change the research positioning.

P1.justification: The prose and section sequence remain largely unchanged. v3 adds a short sensitivity discussion, code-access sentence, acknowledgements and generic impact statement, alongside affiliation and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the single-column main paper and references with a two-column conference layout, adds running headers, reformats equations and Algorithm 1, and resizes or repositions retained figures and tables. It also adds Table 2; Figures 1–4 retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The added smoothing study supplies practical evidence and an explanation for parameter selection that v1 lacked. The repository pointer also improves reproducibility information. These are useful but limited gains: the method, proofs and original benchmark results remain unchanged.
